chunks: Fadalah ibn 'Ukba narrated from al-Aban ibn 'Uthman, from al-Salami ibn Abi Hafs, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, peace be upon them, from Jabir ibn Yazid, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by the market, seeking perfume, while the people surrounded him. He passed by a dead kid goat with cut ears, lying in a rubbish heap, so he took it by its ear and asked, 'Who among you would like this to be his for a dirham?' They said, 'We would not like it to be ours for anything, and what would we do with it?' He said, 'Would you not like it to be yours?' They said, 'No.' He repeated that three times, so they said, 'By Allah, even if it were alive it would be flawed, so how about now when it is dead?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Verily, the world in the sight of Allah is less valuable to you than this [dead goat] is to you.'

key_terms.جدي أسك: A kid goat with cut ears

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith about the value of the world compared to a dead goat?
ai.summary: In this well-known hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) uses a vivid market scene to demonstrate the disparity between human valuation of the world and Divine valuation. By asking the crowd if they would buy a dead, discarded goat for a dirham, and receiving a resounding 'no' even if it were alive, he illustrates that the entire cosmos is of negligible worth to Allah compared to its perceived value to humanity. This narrative underscores the Shia concept of *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere rejection of the world, but as a correct perspective on its transient nature relative to the eternal.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 11.Faḍālah narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Salamah ibn Abī Ḥafṣ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh, from his father (a), from Jābir who said,

“The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) passed by the market and approached [one of the shops] seeking to buy some perfume, while the people had surrounded him. Then he passed by a dead goat with its ears cut, lying in a rubbish heap, so he took hold of it by its [severed] ear and asked, ‘Who among you would want to buy this for a dirham?’ They said, ‘We would not like to buy this for any amount – what would we do with it?’ He said, ‘Would you not like to possess it?’ They said, ‘No!’ He (ṣ) repeated that [question] thrice, so they said, ‘By Allah, even if it were alive it would be flawed, so how about now when it is dead!’ The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said, ‘Verily the [material] world is less valuable to Allah than this [dead goat] is to you.’”
